## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukhavihāra Sutta* ("Living in Happiness", Iti 29; PTS It 23) is a short discourse preserved in the *Dukanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka*. The text teaches that guarding the doors of the sense faculties and knowing moderation in eating lead to ease and happiness both in this life and in future births. The reference passages retrieved in bibliographical searches do not discuss this specific sutta; mentions of *sukhavihāra* in those sources instead concern the standard meditative formula of "dwelling at ease in the present life" (*diṭṭhadhamma-sukhavihāra*) in Abhidharma or the *Sukhavihāra-parivarta* (chapter 14) of the Mahāyāna *Saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra*.

 According to DharmaNexus analysis, the sutta exhibits extensive internal Pali text reuse (97 matching passages across 13 texts) [DharmaNexus]. Its closest partner is its direct counterpart, the *Dukkhavihāra Sutta* (Iti 28), sharing nearly identical formulation across almost the entire text (§0.1–6.1, 91% similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are also shared with discourses in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5, AN 6, AN 3, AN 8), the *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* (DN 30), and other *Itivuttaka* discourses (such as Iti 41 and Iti 37) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated matches, DharmaNexus additionally aligns segments of the discourse with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125, fascicle 12) [DharmaNexus].
